question.problem:
Finding the vertical shift $D$ of the function $y=\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + D.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14256901/assets/24f655be039642475cad1e2a7bf4647004a4dce07dd936b60377b01428f7079e.png)
question.worked_solution:
The constant $D$ represents a vertical shift of the function $y=\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right).$

From the graph, we see that the given curve shifted **down** by $1$ unit. So, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)-1.
$$

Therefore, $D =-1.$
